continuity_anchors: on a flat wooden desk surface under bright, even indoor lighting
video_goal: Demonstrate how to properly sharpen a wooden pencil and empty the shavings tray using a Bostitch Personal Electric Pencil Sharpener.
single_prompt: A Close-up shot establishes a compact black Bostitch Personal Electric Pencil Sharpener with a translucent front shavings tray resting on a flat wooden desk surface under bright, even indoor lighting. The camera pans slightly to highlight the Bostitch logo. Transitioning to an extreme close-up, a hand enters holding a yellow wooden pencil, rotating it to display a broken, flat graphite tip. From an over-the-shoulder view, the hand guides the dull pencil downward toward the circular insertion hole on top of the sharpener. In a close-up, the hand pushes the pencil down into the hole until it stops, keeping a firm grip. The sharpener vibrates slightly on the desk as the hand holds the pencil steady to prevent spinning. A macro view reveals wood and graphite shavings rapidly falling and accumulating inside the front translucent tray. The camera pulls back to a close-up as the hand pulls the pencil straight up and out of the insertion hole. In an extreme close-up, the hand rotates the pencil to display a sharp, pointed graphite tip. A medium shot shows the hand placing the sharpened pencil down on the desk beside the sharpener. Returning to a close-up, the thumb and index finger pinch the textured side grips of the translucent shavings tray and pull it straight out, exposing a pile of fresh shavings. From an over-the-shoulder view, the hand moves the tray over a small wastebasket and tilts it upside down to empty the shavings. Finally, in a close-up, the hand aligns the empty tray with the front opening of the sharpener and pushes it in until it sits flush, leaving the device ready for its next use.
